subject: Hosted inference: transient token surge causing degraded responses — mitigation & next steps
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jiang <sam.jiang@moonlighttech.com>; ops@moonlighttech.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference: transient token surge causing degraded responses — mitigation & next steps

Hi Sam / Moonlight ops team,

Quick heads-up: from ~08:55 PDT we observed a token-rate surge originating from a narrow set of customer API keys in the US-WEST cluster that temporarily pushed KV cache eviction rates above our safety thresholds. Symptoms we saw that may affect you: elevated p95/p99 generation latency, a small fraction (<0.8%) of truncated responses, and intermittent 503s for burst requests.

We routed additional capacity and applied an emergency rate-adaptive limiter at 09:04 PDT which brought tail latency back down. Root cause appears to be a customer-side workload pattern that amplified prefix cache churn; we are still validating whether a recent SDK change increased client reconnects.

Immediate ask for Moonlight Tech: if you can, please confirm whether you are able to temporarily enable "allow_model_variant_fallback" on your integration (we can flip this on server-side for you). That will route heavy short-lived requests to a compatible higher-memory variant which avoids repeated KV lookups and should eliminate truncation.

We attached a short incident summary and will publish the status page incident entry once this thread is visible to your team. Proposed next steps:
- We keep the permissive fallback enabled for 48 hours while we monitor (opt-out available).
- Postmortem + timeline call the week of Jun 28 (30 mins) — propose Tue 06/29 10:00 PDT or Wed 06/30 14:00 PDT.

Attachments: incident_summary_20270621.log (short), mitigation_runbook_20270621.pdf (runbook & rollback steps).

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll keep you updated within 1h or on any material changes.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai

Please go ahead and enable the fallback for our account; we'd prefer to avoid client-side changes while we triage. Also two quick questions:
1) ETA on when the permissive fallback will be in place for us?
2) Are you expecting any billing adjustments / SLA credit discussions for the affected window?

We'd like the postmortem call on Tue 06/29 10:00 PDT if that works.

Sam

Subject: Re: Hosted inference: transient token surge causing degraded responses — mitigation & next steps

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 09:36 AM Sam Jiang <sam.jiang@moonlighttech.com> wrote:
> Thanks Maya — we did see an uptick in 503s around ~08:58 and some truncated completions in our logs.
> Please go ahead and enable the fallback for our account; we'd prefer to avoid client-side changes while we triage. Also two quick questions:
> 1) ETA on when the permissive fallback will be in place for us?
> 2) Are you expecting any billing adjustments / SLA credit discussions for the affected window?

Hi Sam — thanks for confirming.

1) ETA: I’ve enabled the permissive fallback for your account at 10:09 PDT. You should see immediate improvement; please restart any persistent connections or refresh your SDK token cache to pick up the variant routing. We will monitor p95/p99 and truncated response counts for the next 48 hours and will disable the fallback earlier if signal stabilizes.

2) Billing / SLA: we are tracking the full timeline and will include a proposed credit calculation in the postmortem. Early note: the affected period was ~08:55–09:04 PDT for the elevated errors, and broader tail latency until ~09:12 PDT for a subset of long-running requests. We will provide a more detailed impact report and proposed credits in the formal postmortem doc.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2027-06-21-token-surge (we pushed the initial incident entry at 09:22 PDT).

Next: postmortem call Tue 06/29 10:00 PDT confirmed. Agenda will be: timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations (short-term and platform changes), client recommendations, and credit proposal.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the full runbook excerpt and data in the hour.

Best,
Maya

Attachments referenced: mitigation_runbook_20270621.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: post-incident next steps for token-surge event (Moonlight)

Internal note — adding short ops items for follow-up before the postmortem call:
- Extract SDK reconnect traces for the three keys that manifested the highest churn (task: ops-trace-548, owner: Evelyn).
- Validate whether recent client-side keepalive change correlates with reconnect spikes (team: integrations).
- Schedule kernel selection review for US-WEST pinned variants (owner: infra-models).
- Draft provisional SLA credit calc (Olga), include per-token unit exposure and 1-week lookback normalization.

I’ll package the data into the postmortem doc and share a draft by Fri 06/25 EOD.

Evelyn
